newsitem.title: USA: Amax Gold output rate of 700,000 oz in '97.
newsitem.headline: Amax Gold output rate of 700,000 oz in '97.

text.p: Amax Gold Inc is expected to produce gold at the rate of 700,000 ounces a year in the second quarter of this year with all three of its new projects on stream, said Milton Ward, president, chairman and CEO of Cyprus Amax Minerals, Amax Gold's majority owner.
Ward told an analyst teleconference that Amax Gold's wholly-owned Fort Knox mine poured its first gold in December and will enter commercial production this quarter.
The Refugio mine in Chile, 50 percent owned by Amax Gold, the rest by Bema Gold Corp has entered full production, and the Kubaka mine in Russia, will also produce its first gold this quarter.
Bema said on Wednesday that output at Refugio will rise to 500,000 ounces by the year 2000 from current design capacity of 230,000 ounces.
Ward declined to comment on Bema's forecast.
Cyprus owns 52.5 percent of Amax Gold, and this share will increase to 59.1 percent in February when Amax will own half of Kubaka once the ownership is transferred from Cyprus.
The balance of Kubaka is owned by Russian partners.
Ward reiterated that he wanted Amax Gold to grow and the best way would be by linking with a partner.

Cyprus would probably end up owning less of Amax Gold, but the deconsolidation of Amax Gold would take about $450 million of debt away from Cyprus Amax and lessen its interest payments by $35 to $40 million a year, to "make a big difference in our balance sheet".
Amax Gold has outlined 7 million ounces of gold resources in addition to its reserve base and it will start drilling to to convert those resources into reserves.
Of the 7 million ounces of resources, some 3 million ounces are at Refugio, 1.5 million at Fort Knox, and the balance at Kubaka.
